10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing FNAF-style browser game into a complete, higher-quality playable horror experience optimized for modern phones.

## Requirements
- Improve graphics quality substantially.
- Prevent doors from visually passing through walls.
- Optimize presentation for high-detail phones such as Google Pixel 9.
- Make the game scarier.
- Make power drain substantially slower than before.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game.
- Used a detailed dark office, fixed wall/door geometry, high-DPI canvas scaling, animated enemies, camera feeds, and dramatic UI.
- Power loss was made gradual and dependent on active systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the complete game interface in `index.html`.
- Added responsive high-quality visual styling in `styles.css`.
- Added a canvas-rendered office, clipped door bays, animated creature silhouettes, desk, monitor, and environmental effects in `game.js`.
- Added live camera feeds, multiple rooms, enemy progression, survival timer, power system, sound effects, keyboard and touch controls, and win/lose states.
- Fixed the door implementation so moving leaves remain inside their wall openings.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the project and perform browser screenshots for visual verification.
2. Test gameplay on mobile viewport dimensions and adjust if needed.
3. Verify that the 6 AM win condition and enemy attack timing are balanced.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Fnafv2/Fnafv2/index.html`: Main game structure and UI.
- `/home/runner/work/Fnafv2/Fnafv2/styles.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `/home/runner/work/Fnafv2/Fnafv2/game.js`: Rendering, enemy AI, power mechanics, controls, and game states.

## Important Context
- The implementation is currently untracked; no commits or pushes were made.
- The workspace had no existing application files before the generated build.
